explain.say: A zip has two rows of teeth on fabric tapes, and a slider that runs up and down them. The slider does all the work; you just pull it.

explain.say: Inside, the slider has a Y-shaped passage. Pulling it up squeezes the two rows from the arms of the Y into the single channel at the bottom.

explain.say: The teeth on one side sit between the teeth on the other. The channels tilt each tooth so the bump on its top slots into the hollow under the tooth above, and the rows lock together.

faq.q: What does the zip slider do?
faq.a: The slider has a Y-shaped channel inside. Pulled up, it brings the two rows of teeth together at just the right angle to lock. Pulled down, its wedge separates them.
asks: How does a zip slider work?

faq.q: Why is the slider shaped like a Y?
faq.a: The two arms of the Y take one row of teeth each, and the narrow stem forces them together. The narrowing curve is what pushes the teeth into place.
asks: What is inside a zip slider?

faq.q: How do the zip teeth lock together?
faq.a: Each tooth has a bump on top and a hollow underneath. As the teeth mesh, each bump fits the hollow of a tooth on the other side, so the rows hold together.

faq.q: How does a zip come undone?
faq.a: A small wedge between the arms of the Y pushes the meshed teeth apart and tilts them so the bumps come out of the hollows.
asks: Why does pulling down open a zip?

faq.a: Whitcomb Judson made a clasp fastener in 1893, and Gideon Sundback designed the modern zip with interlocking teeth in 1913. The name zipper came from a 1923 boot.

facts: Gideon Sundback designed the modern interlocking zip in 1913.
Many zips are marked YKK, from a Japanese company that makes a large share of the world's zips.

quiz.say: What separates the teeth when you pull a zip open?
quiz.show: What separates the teeth when you pull a zip open?
quiz.why: A wedge between the arms of the slider's Y-channel prises the teeth apart.

wrong.2: The fabric does not open the teeth; the slider does.
